channel.title: Global Arbitration Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Arbitration Review (globalarbitrationreview.com)

item.title: Top Dutch court upholds enforcement of Indian satellite award
item.description: The Dutch Supreme Court has upheld the enforcement of a US$1.4 billion ICC award against an Indian state-owned entity even though the award has been annulled in India on grounds of fraud.

item.title: Omni Bridgeway gets all-clear to target Albanian assets
item.description: A US court has given Australian funder Omni Bridgeway leave to begin efforts to attach assets belonging to Albania and its national oil company so it can execute a US$15 million ICC award.

item.title: LCIA opens consultation on its rules
item.description: The London Court of International Arbitration has launched a public consultation on potential changes to its arbitration rules, six years after they were last revised.

item.title: Hungarian investor pursues ECT claim against Spain
item.description: A Hungarian state-backed consortium is pursuing an Energy Charter Treaty claim against Spain over the government’s decision to block its takeover of a Spanish train manufacturer.

item.title: Gazprom fails to undo billion-dollar Naftogaz award
item.description: The Swiss Federal Tribunal has refused Gazprom’s bid to set aside an ICC award ordering it to pay US$1.37 billion to Ukrainian state entity Naftogaz under a contract for the transit of Russian gas through Ukraine.

item.title: Mishcon and Gateley hire Middle East practice heads
item.description: Mishcon de Reya has hired Bushra Ahmed in Dubai as head of its Middle East disputes practice, while former Charles Russell Speechlys partner Alim Khamis has taken up the same role at Gateley.

item.title: Niger state entity beats bid to revive uranium claim
item.description: The Swiss Federal Tribunal has rejected a Cyprus-registered uranium trader’s bid to revive a nearly US$200 million ICC claim against a Niger state entity.

item.title: British arbitrator accused of serious conflict in SIAC case
item.description: A US$500 million SIAC award against India's Tata group has come under the spotlight, amid disputed allegations that one of the arbitrators, a British King's Counsel, had engaged in "dubious" business dealings in Russia with the winning side's owner and chief witness.

item.title: Hong Kong court hears Russia’s challenge to arbitrator in BIT case
item.description: A Hong Kong court is hearing Russia’s challenge to an arbitrator appointed by a German company in a bilateral investment treaty claim administered by the HKIAC – the same arbitrator having already been removed from a parallel Energy Charter Treaty case.
